messages.subject: Re: novice issue with installation
parts:
I think you need to tweak your LoadModule path to mod_R.so. It'd
probably be best if you read:

http://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.2/mod/mod_so.html#loadmodule

I think the server directory is prepended to whatever you place in LoadModule.

Jeff

messages.author: 98e634f62928ae87
messages.subject: Re: novice issue with installation
parts:
If you have `locate` installed, you can find any file on your system.

E.g. on Ubuntu with standard RApache installation `locate mod_R.so` returns:

/usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so

Best,
Gergely

On Fri, Dec 21, 2012 at 8:44 PM, <yif...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have the same problem, but it seems related to the line in configuration file httpd.conf ( apache2.conf ? in Mint/Ubuntu):

LoadModule R_module /apache/module/path/mod_R.so

My question is where to fine the mod_R.so ?

Thanks a lot!

YT

On Friday, June 8, 2012 3:36:35 PM UTC-6, whey wrote:
I'm having trouble with the shared object issue that is well documented in 3.1 of the manual. I am running Fedora 15, using R 2.15.0. I am pretty certain that I have:

1) installed R for use as a shared library via that flag in ./configure.
2) successfully installed rapache.
3) added the R_module line to the Apache configuration file:

# cat /usr/local/apache2/conf/httpd.conf | grep R_module
LoadModule R_module /apache/module/path/mod_R.so

4) edited /etc/ld.so.conf and run ldconfig as root:

# ldconfig -v | grep libR
        libRblas.so -> libRblas.so
        libR.so -> libR.so
        libRlapack.so -> libRlapack.so

Yet:

# /usr/local/apache2/bin/apachectl -k start
httpd: Syntax error on line 147 of /usr/local/apache2/conf/httpd.conf: Cannot load /apache/module/path/mod_R.so into server: /apache/module/path/mod_R.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory


Note that the apache install works without rapache, or at least the command to start apache works and http://localhost has that "It works!" page. I'm a bit of a unix novice so it's possible I've missed something obvious. Any thoughts? Thanks.

--

parts:
Hi Jonathan

If you're on Ubuntu, just use the installation package:

sudo add-apt-repository opencpu/rapache
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install libapache2-mod-r-base
